item.text:
**4B.8 Research Note: Bola Ahmed Tinubu (2024)**

Bottom line: I found no 2024 evidence that Tinubu tried to extend his own term, rewrite succession rules, or obstruct a constitutional transfer of power. The closest positive evidence is constitutional-reform rhetoric and ordinary cabinet management. The negative side is stronger on coalition erosion and punitive treatment of opposition mobilization, which raises one-party-state risk but still falls short of a direct term-limit violation.

- **[President Tinubu Receives Patriot Group, Says Strengthening Nigeria’s Economy a Topmost Priority but Request for New Constitution Will Be Reviewed](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-receives-patriot-group-says-strengthening-nigerias-economy-a-topmost-priority-but-request-for-new-constitution-will-be-reviewed/)** — State House, August 9, 2024. Tinubu said the request for a constituent assembly and new constitution would be reviewed, and he framed constitutional change as the way to manage diversity and avoid “conflicts and break-ups.” This is the strongest direct 2024 sign that he preferred constitutional channels over extra-constitutional rule changes. QIDs: `4B.8`.

- **[Tinubu’s call for collaboration on governance splits opposition parties](https://guardian.ng/politics/tinubus-call-for-collaboration-on-governance-splits-opposition-parties/)** — The Guardian Nigeria, January 7, 2024. Tinubu’s New Year message said, “Election is over. It’s time for all of us to work together,” which is a pro-coalition, post-election-unity signal. At the same time, opposition reactions warned that this could drift into a one-party state, so the item cuts both ways. QIDs: `4B.8`, `4B.5`.

- **[Nigeria’s Tinubu names seven ministers, sacks five in cabinet reshuffle](https://theprint.in/world/nigerias-tinubu-names-seven-ministers-sacks-five-in-cabinet-reshuffle/2325625/)** — Reuters via ThePrint, October 23, 2024. Reuters described a standard cabinet reshuffle, with some ministers removed, others swapped, and key ministries retained. That is weak positive evidence against arbitrary purge or loyalty-testing behavior, but it does not prove durable respect for coalition commitments. QIDs: `4B.8`, `4B.5`.

- **[Anti-govt protest: LP denies involvement as Presidency fingers Obi, alleges treason](https://punchng.com/anti-govt-protest-lp-denies-involvement-as-presidency-fingers-obi-alleges-treason/)** — Punch, July 21, 2024. The presidency reportedly cast anti-government protest hashtags and Peter Obi supporters as “treasonable” and “anarchists,” which treats opposition mobilization as subversion rather than legitimate political contestation. This is negative evidence for respect for opposition space and coalition pluralism. QIDs: `4B.8`, `4B.5`, `4B.1`.

- **[Nigeria charges protesters with treason, inciting military](https://theprint.in/world/nigeria-charges-protesters-with-treason-inciting-military/2249248/)** — Reuters via ThePrint, September 2, 2024. Prosecutors charged protesters with treason and mutiny and alleged they intended to destabilize the country, using criminal law to escalate against dissent. That undercuts the case that Tinubu’s government was fully tolerant of constitutional opposition or orderly political turnover. QIDs: `4B.8`, `4B.5`, `4B.3`.

- **[Nigeria charges 76 including minors with treason after August protests](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/nigeria-charges-76-including-minors-with-treason-after-august-protests-3698000)** — Reuters via Investing.com, November 1, 2024. Reuters reported the case expanded to 76 defendants, including minors, after the August protests, reinforcing the picture of punitive escalation and collective punishment. This is negative for succession/transfer norms only indirectly, but it strongly supports the broader one-party-state / intimidation reading. QIDs: `4B.8`, `4B.5`, `4B.7`.

Search gap: I did not find a 2024 source showing Tinubu attempted a third term, altered succession rules, blocked an election transfer, or explicitly violated coalition agreements. The evidence is therefore indirect: constitutional-reform language on the positive side, and coalition-concentration / repression signals on the negative side.
